extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers (researchers who review manuscripts for journals/conferences)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for reviewers to distinguish and carry out two roles: gatekeeping (deciding if a manuscript meets venue standards) and editing (providing constructive, developmental feedback to improve the manuscript). Advice applies to reviewers and editors across academic fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Deciding whether work meets publication standards for the venue. Subjective judgment about what's 'good enough.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly to the editor whether the manuscript is fundamentally sound or unsound; assess fit for the journal/venue. This is the decision-making role (accept/reject/major revision) rather than detailed developmental help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing (constructive, developmental feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing constructive feedback to strengthen the manuscript — 'big picture advice' like restructuring arguments or suggesting additional analyses, not merely listing typos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give suggestions that improve clarity, argumentation, analysis, and contribution. Focus on substantive fixes (restructure, additional analyses, clearer framing) rather than only copyediting. Even if recommending rejection, identify ways the authors could make the paper better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate and report the three-part judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete review separates: (a) is this fundamentally sound?, (b) is it the right venue?, (c) what would make it stronger?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the review to make those three elements explicit so editors and authors can see the gatekeeping decision and the developmental advice independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of fundamental soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the editor and authors clearly whether the work is 'fundamentally sound or unsound' and give detailed rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not bury the basic accept/reject assessment in prose. Provide the rationale (major flaws or reasons for confidence) so the editor can weigh your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 3–5 most important improvements on rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when rejecting a paper, identify '3-5 most important things they can do to improve.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the key changes that would most increase the manuscript's publishability; this is actionable, targeted advice rather than a laundry list of minor issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and cultivate 'diamonds in the rough'
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify manuscripts with strong potential despite current flaws and be willing to work through multiple revision rounds when the potential exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper has a valuable contribution, consider recommending revision and offering developmental guidance rather than outright rejection. Editors/reviewers who can both gatekeep and edit add value here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on contributions, not just flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should emphasize the paper's contributions and how they matter, not merely catalogue problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what the paper adds to the field and suggest ways to better articulate or strengthen that contribution, which helps editors and authors see the value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid brevity-only reviews (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity-only reviews—brief rejections without developmental feedback—are deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantive reasoning and at least some guidance; short 'reject' notes without explanation are unhelpful to editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure cheerleading (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure cheerleading—praise without critical evaluation or concrete suggestions—is also deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance positive comments with constructive criticism and concrete suggestions for improvement; unexplained praise doesn't help editors decide or authors revise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to perform both roles when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and editors who combine gatekeeping and editing functions are ideal — 'that rare gift.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to give a clear decision-oriented judgment while also offering developmental advice; treating the roles as orthogonal allows you to do both.
